parole.significato: Forming adjectives from nouns, indicating that something belongs to, resembles, is characterized by, is suited for, or…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Germanic *-īnaz (“belonging to, characterized by, made of”), an adjective-forming suffix. Compare Norwegian Nynorsk -en, Danish -en, Swedish -en, German -en and English -en (“adjective-forming suffix”).

parole.significato: a holofoil trading card
parole.testo: From glinse. Cognate with Norwegian Bokmål glans, through Proto-Germanic *glend-.

parole.significato: a blackfly (any member of the Simuliidae)
parole.testo: Cognate with Swedish knott, English gnat and maybe Russian гнус (gnus). Inherited from Proto-Germanic *gnattaz

parole.significato: flea (a wingless parasitical insect)
parole.testo: From Proto-Germanic *luppǭ (“flea, sandflea”, originally “jumper”), from Proto-Germanic *luppijaną (“to jump, dart”).

parole.significato: a lung
parole.testo: From Proto-Germanic *lungô (“the light organ”), from Proto-Indo-European *lengʷʰ- (“light, agile, nimble”). Compare Dutch long, English lung, Danish lunge, German Lunge, Swedish lunga, Icelandic lunga.

parole.significato: a nose
parole.testo: From Proto-Germanic *nasō, from Proto-Indo-European *néh₂s-, and Old Norse nǫs.

parole.significato: rust; a reddish-brown coating of hydrated iron oxides or iron hydroxides formed on iron or steel through oxidation
parole.testo: Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *rustaz (“rust”), from Proto-Indo-European *rudʰso- (“red”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rewdʰ- (“red”). Related to rød (“red”). Compare Norwegian Nynorsk rust, Danish rust, Swedish rost, Dutch roest, German Rost and English rust.

parole.significato: a schilling, the old currency of Austria, divided into 100 groschen
parole.testo: Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *skillingaz. Doublet of shilling and skilling.

parole.significato: the act or process of setting, placing, or deploying something
parole.testo: From sette (“to set, put, place”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *satjaną (“to set, place”), from Proto-Indo-European *sodéyeti (“to cause to sit”), the causative of *sed- (“to sit”). parole.significato: skin
parole.testo: From Proto-Germanic *skinþą, and Old Norse skinn.

parole.significato: to glance, especially quickly, sideways, or furtively

parole.significato: a wasp (insect)
parole.testo: From Proto-Germanic *wepsō-, from Proto-Indo-European *wobʰseh₂ (“wasp”), from *webʰ- (“weave”). Compare Danish hveps.

parole.significato: to shovel (something)
parole.testo: Either denominal from etymology 1 or directly from the underlying Middle Low German schûven (“to push”), from Proto-Germanic *skeubaną.

parole.significato: the top (highest point)
parole.testo: From Old Norse toppr, from Proto-Germanic *tuppaz (“tuft, top, summit”), either a secondary formation from *tebō, *tappaz (“tuft, knot, peg”), or from earlier *tumpaz with irregular development *mp > *pp, from Proto-Indo-European *dewmb- (“penis, tail, rod”).

parole.significato: warm, hot
parole.testo: From Old Norse varmr, from Proto-Germanic *warmaz, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰer- (“warm, hot”) or alternatively *wer- (“to burn”).

parole.significato: vegan (not containing animal products (meat, eggs, milk, leather, etc) or inherently involving animal use)
parole.testo: From vegan + -sk, first part from English vegan, a clipping of either vegetarian or vegetable. Last part from Old Norse -skr, from Proto-Germanic *-iskaz, from Proto-Indo-European *-iskos.
